title: When Stupid Was a Diagnosis
gist: Alice Fleerackers recounts how late-1800s physicians treated pregnancy vomiting as a harbinger of lifelong "idiocy," attributing this "poverty of the mind" to causes ranging from neurotic parents to the weather and at the extreme to moral failure. Her stated stake is that this history is in danger of returning as support for people with disabilities withers; the piece is cut off at the paywall before that argument is developed.

insights.claim: In the late 1800s some doctors interpreted vomiting during pregnancy not as a symptom but as the harbinger of a lifelong debilitating condition in the unborn child, which they called "idiocy."
insights.speaker: Alice Fleerackers
insights.so_what: A concrete case of a common physiological sign being converted into a permanent diagnostic label — the failure pattern to watch as new predictive screening tools scale.

insights.claim: Hypothesized causes of so-called "poverty of the mind" in the late 1800s ranged across neurotic parents, the weather and pregnancy vomiting, with beliefs rapidly evolving rather than settling.
insights.speaker: Alice Fleerackers
insights.so_what: Rapidly rotating causal stories with stable diagnostic labels is the signature of an unmoored classification system — a diagnostic-inflation tell.

insights.claim: Some 19th-century medical professionals framed "idiocy" as a moral failure, treating it as evidence that children or their parents had violated natural laws so far that their bodies could no longer house the powers of the soul.
insights.speaker: Alice Fleerackers
insights.so_what: Shows how a clinical label can carry moral desert, which is the mechanism by which entitlement to support gets withdrawn.
insights.quote: so far violated the natural laws
insights.locator: At the extreme, some medical professionals even saw idiocy as a moral failure

insights.claim: The author's stated concern is that the history of diagnosing intellectual disability as moral failure is in danger of returning as support for people with disabilities withers.
insights.speaker: Alice Fleerackers
insights.so_what: Frames disability-support retrenchment as a live policy direction — relevant to social-services, special-education and long-term-care exposure.
insights.quote: A dark history that is in danger of returning as support for people with disabilities withers
